newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound two Arabs in West Bank clash.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound two Arabs in West Bank clash.

text.p: Israeli soldiers fired rubber bullets at Palestinian demonstrators in the West Bank on Sunday, lightly wounding two, the army said.

An army spokesman said soldiers at a checkpoint near a Jewish settlement east of Tel Aviv opened fire to quell protests that erupted after soldiers detained two Arabs trying to enter Israel without work permits.

"Two Palestinians were lightly wounded this morning during riots near the Oranit settlement. Soldiers in the area dispersed the demonstration with...rubber bullets which wounded the Palestinians," the spokesman said.

Tensions have been high in the West Bank and Gaza, occupied by Israel in 1967, since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu approved the building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on Wednesday.
Palestinians have warned that the decision to build 6,500 Jewish homes on a tree-covered East Jerusalem hill could lead to bloodshed.
Israel views all of Jerusalem as its capital. Palestinians want the city's eastern half, taken by Israel in 1967, as the capital of an independent state.

In a move to ease tensions in the West Bank, Israeli occupation authorities decided to temporarily halt demolitions of illegally built Arab homes in West Bank areas under its control, security sources said.
